places.title: Places of Interest
places.subtitle: Discover the hidden treasures and wonders of Pisa

items.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
items.description: The famous inclined bell tower of the 12th century, symbol of Pisa and icon of Italy in the world. About 56 meters high with 294 steps, it offers breathtaking panoramic views from the top after climbing its characteristic stairs.

items.name: Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta
items.description: Majestic Romanesque cathedral built from 1064 with white and gray marble facade. The interior with white and black bands houses masterpieces like Cimabue's apsidal mosaic and Giovanni Pisano's Gothic pulpit.

items.name: Baptistery of St. John
items.description: Imposing circular baptistery in Romanesque-Gothic style from 1153, the largest in Italy. Famous for its exceptional acoustics and prolonged echo, it houses an elegant baptismal font and Nicola Pisano's sculpted pulpit.

items.name: Monumental Cemetery
items.description: Ancient historic cemetery with porticoes, built with earth from Jerusalem brought by the crusaders. The walls were adorned with 14th-century frescoes like the Triumph of Death, now partially restored.

items.name: Church of Santa Maria della Spina
items.description: Small Gothic church from 1230 facing the Lungarno, considered a jewel of Italian Gothic architecture. It owes its name to a relic of the thorn from Christ's crown, with richly decorated facade featuring spires, rose windows and polychrome marble statues.

items.name: Piazza dei Cavalieri
items.description: Elegant Renaissance square designed by Giorgio Vasari for Cosimo I de' Medici. Former center of Pisan civil power, today it faces the Palazzo della Carovana (seat of the Scuola Normale Superiore) with frescoed facade and the Church of Santo Stefano dei Cavalieri.

items.name: Borgo Stretto and Lungarni
items.description: Picturesque medieval street in the city center and scenic avenues along the Arno. Borgo Stretto is flanked by medieval porticoes with historic shops and cafes, while the Lungarni offer rows of historic palaces with colored facades and romantic evening views.

items.name: National Museum of San Matteo
items.description: One of Pisa's most important museums, housing numerous masterpieces of painting and sculpture from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance. The collection includes works by Tuscan artists like Nicola and Giovanni Pisano and precious 14th and 15th-century panels.

items.name: Palazzo Blu
items.description: Historic palace on the Lungarno, seat of an art museum and cultural center. It houses permanent collections with over 300 works from the 14th to 20th centuries including paintings, archaeological finds and numismatics, plus prestigious international temporary exhibitions.

items.name: Museum of Ancient Ships
items.description: Modern archaeological museum in the Medici Arsenals, dedicated to Roman ships found in Pisa. It displays seven restored Roman-era vessels (3rd BC - 7th AD) and about 8,000 artifacts, offering a glimpse into ancient maritime Pisa.

items.name: Botanical Garden and Museum
items.description: Historic botanical garden founded in 1544, the world's first university botanical garden. It houses tropical greenhouses, an arboretum with centuries-old plants and collections of rare plants. The small museum displays botanical specimens and period plant anatomical waxes.

items.name: Keith Haring's 'Tuttomondo' Mural
items.description: Large contemporary art mural created in 1989 by artist Keith Haring on the external wall of the Church of S. Antonio Abate. The colorful 180 m² work depicts 30 stylized figures symbolizing peace and harmony in the world.

items.name: Cathedral Museum
items.description: Houses original medieval sculptures, paintings and treasures from the monuments of Piazza dei Miracoli, including masterpieces by Giovanni Pisano and other Pisan masters. A journey through the art that made Pisa famous worldwide.

items.name: Sinopie Museum
items.description: Unique exhibition of preparatory drawings (sinopie) of the ancient frescoes of the Camposanto, such as those of the Triumph of Death. It allows you to appreciate the technical 'behind the scenes' of 14th-century Pisan frescoes.

events.title: Info Events
events.subtitle: Don't miss the most interesting appointments in the city

items.name: Pisan New Year
items.description: Historic-religious reenactment celebrating the ancient Pisan calendar, according to which the new year begins on March 25th. A historic procession crosses the city to the Cathedral, where at noon a ray of sun penetrating from the dome symbolically marks the entrance into the new year.

items.name: Luminara di San Ranieri
items.description: City festival in honor of patron saint San Ranieri: on the evening of June 16th, over 100,000 wax candles illuminate all the palaces along the Lungarni, creating a magical atmosphere. The night concludes with spectacular fireworks over the river.

items.name: Palio di San Ranieri (Historical Regatta)
items.description: Historic rowing regatta on the Arno between the four ancient districts of Pisa (San Francesco, San Martino, Santa Maria and Sant'Antonio). Takes place in the afternoon of San Ranieri's day: costumed crews compete on fanghi boats going up the river, evoking Pisan maritime traditions.

items.name: Game of the Bridge
items.description: Spectacular costumed reenactment of a medieval battle on the Ponte di Mezzo. The city divides into the historic factions of Tramontana and Mezzogiorno: after a procession of over 700 16th-century armed men, the teams face off pushing a cart along the bridge.

items.name: Pisa Book Festival
items.description: Festival dedicated to independent publishing with national and international guests, translation awards, poetry focus and activities for young readers. An unmissable appointment for lovers of literary culture.

items.name: Internet Festival - Forms of Future
items.description: Event dedicated to internet, digital culture, technology, digital ethics and innovation. Promoted by CNR, University of Pisa, Region and other institutions, it represents a national reference point for digital culture.

items.name: Anima Mundi Festival
items.description: Classical and sacred music concerts often in the scenic setting of Piazza dei Miracoli or other symbolic places in the city. A unique musical experience that combines art and spirituality.
